title: Cultural and Technological Determinants of OnlineGrocery Shopping Among Ethnic Consumers in theUnited Kingdom

detail.title: Cultural and Technological Determinants of OnlineGrocery Shopping Among Ethnic Consumers in theUnited Kingdom
detail.abstract: The rapid growth of online grocery shopping has transformed consumer purchasing behaviour; however, limited research has examined how ethnic consumers engage with online grocery platforms in the United Kingdom. Given the increasing size and economic significance of ethnic minority populations, understanding their online grocery shopping behaviour is both theoretically and practically important. This study investigates the influence of cultural, attitudinal, technological, trust-related, risk-related, and demographic factors on ethnic consumers’ online grocery shopping behaviour.A quantitative research design was adopted using survey data collected from 365 ethnic consumers in the UK. Statistical analyses, including correlation analysis, multiple regression, t-tests, and ANOVA were employed to test hypotheses derived from consumer behaviour and technology adoption theories.The findings indicate that cultural satisfaction, responsiveness to culturally aligned promotional offers, favourable consumer attitudes, and culturally aligned website design positively influence online grocery shopping behaviour among ethnic consumers. Perceived risk was found to negatively influence purchase decision-making, while trust significantly predicts online grocery shopping intention. Contrary to assumptions in some prior literature, ethnic consumers did not demonstrate pronounced technological adaptation barriers to adopting online grocery platforms. Demographic analysis indicates that age and education influence adoption behaviour, while gender differences were not statistically significant.This study contributes to electronic commerce research by developing a culturally grounded framework explaining online grocery shopping behaviour among ethnic minority consumers. The findings highlight the importance of cultural alignment, risk reduction strategies, and inclusive digital retail environments for engaging diverse consumer segments in the UK online grocery market.

title: Comparative Analysis of Nutrients in Amaranth (Amaranthus Spp.) Grain and Orange Fleshed Sweet Potato (Ipomoea Batata Lam) Varieties Grown in Malawi: Potential Candidate Crops for Infant Diet Formulation
affiliations: Mzuzu University, Mzuzu University, affiliation not provided to SSRN, University of Dar es Salaam, affiliation not provided to SSRN, University of Bonn, Mzuzu University and Mzuzu University

detail.title: Comparative Analysis of Nutrients in Amaranth (Amaranthus Spp.) Grain and Orange Fleshed Sweet Potato (Ipomoea Batata Lam) Varieties Grown in Malawi: Potential Candidate Crops for Infant Diet Formulation
detail.abstract: Malnutrition in infants and young children remains a major public health challenge in Malawi and across sub-Saharan Africa, contributing to stunting, impaired cognitive development, and increased mortality. This study evaluated the nutritional potential and safety of indigenous Amaranthus (A) grain species (A. australis, A. hybridus, A. hypochondriacus) and orange-fleshed sweet potato (OFSP) varieties cultivated in Malawi as candidate ingredients for fortified complementary infant flours. Proximate composition, essential minerals (calcium (Ca), iron (Fe), zinc (Zn), magnesium (Mg)), beta-carotene (provitamin A), vitamin C, bioactive compounds (polyphenols, tannins), and heavy metals were analyzed using standardized AOAC and spectrophotometric methods. Significant compositional variability was observed among species and varieties. A. grains contained high protein (17.79–22.92 g/100 g) and were particularly rich in Fe (18.14–23.88 mg/100 g), Zn (21.38–26.38 mg/100 g), Ca (206.00–434.67 mg/100 g), and Mg (245.47–253.80 mg/100 g), with measurable levels of vitamin C. OFSP varieties were characterized by high moisture (54.20–68.78%), low fat (1.76–2.54 g/100 g), and substantial beta-carotene (10.62–18.17 mg/100 g) and vitamin C (3.12–4.79 mg/100 g) contents. Antinutritional factors were within acceptable ranges, and heavy metals were below regulatory limits, indicating safety for infant food applications. The complementary nutrient profiles of Amaranthus grains and OFSP highlight their synergistic potential for developing affordable, nutrient-dense complementary foods. These findings support the use of locally available, climate-resilient crops as sustainable strategies to improve early-life nutrition and address micronutrient deficiencies in resource-limited settings.

title: Revisiting Global Food Security from a Systems Science Perspective
affiliations: Beijing Normal University, Université de Toulouse, Beijing Normal University, Beijing Normal University, Fuzhou University and Beijing Normal University

detail.title: Revisiting Global Food Security from a Systems Science Perspective
detail.abstract: Global food insecurity is increasingly shaped not by isolated failures in production or access, but by structural transformations that have reconfigured the global food system. Dietary convergence, homogenized production systems, and highly concentrated trade networks have enhanced efficiency and short-term supply stability, yet simultaneously reduced diversity, redundancy, and adaptive capacity. We argue that this transformation has generated an efficiency-vulnerability paradox: the very mechanisms that optimize productivity and specialization amplify systemic exposure to environmental, economic, and geopolitical shocks. Conceptualizing the food system as a tightly coupled, multi-layered network linking consumption, production, and trade, we show how homogenization and structural concentration increase the likelihood of cascading disruptions across scales. In such systems, resilience depends less on output maximization than on structural diversity and coordinated governance. We therefore propose a systems science framework integrating systemic risk diagnosis, multi-actor coordination, and modelling approaches to support adaptive food security governance under increasing uncertainty. Reframing food security through this lens shifts attention from short-term efficiency gains toward long-term resilience and structural robustness in an era of deepening global interdependence.
